headline: Intel has launched robot software and a single-chip platform aimed at running a factory robot's real-time control and AI together.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a company platform launch with unproven performance claims.
importance_line: It affects robot makers and factory owners choosing between Intel and Nvidia, and the claims come from Intel with no independent production results yet.
summary: Tech Times reports that Intel unveiled its Robotics AI Suite and Physical AI Studio at a workshop in Seoul on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, pitching its Core Ultra Series 3 processor, which puts a general processor, graphics unit and AI unit on one chip, as a single-chip alternative to separate controllers and accelerators in factory robots. Tech Times notes that Intel's survey figures are company-commissioned and that production deployments, not workshop claims, will settle how it compares with Nvidia's established Isaac robotics platform.
notes: Category set to ROB (robot platform); no machine shown doing a task, so machine_action false.
